text:
rachel: Observed a reconnect surge after the console rollout that tightened the "resume_tolerance_ms" to 250. Clients emitting partial SSE frames were being closed and immediately resuming, producing back-to-back resume events. Some tenants reported duplicate billing.

ben: Do we have a compact example from the stream parser logs?

rachel: Snippet from sse-proxy: 
```
2026-08-12T11:07:13Z WARN sse_partial_frame session=sess-77 bytes=128 parse_state=trailing_comma
2026-08-12T11:07:13Z INFO connection_close session=sess-77 reason=parser_err
2026-08-12T11:07:13Z INFO resume_request session=sess-77 token=tkn-7 route=eu-central
2026-08-12T11:07:13Z INFO route_switch session=sess-77 new_route=fast-path
2026-08-12T11:07:13Z INFO resume_request session=sess-77 token=tkn-7 route=fast-path
```
Looks like the parser hit partial JSON and closed. The console's smaller resume_tolerance made the system attempt immediate resume instead of waiting for client backoff.

igor: Billing pipeline currently treats resume_request at the edge as the charge signal. If we get two in quick succession and runtime ACKs only the second, customers saw two charges.

maya: Telemetry also hurt triage: the metric-forwarder stripped unknown labels (console_cohort and parser_mode) during rollout so we couldn't filter by canary.

ben: Short-term mitigation: 1) Set resume_tolerance_ms back to 2000 for canary via runtime config; 2) Server-side debounce: ignore identical session+token resume within 2s and suppress billing emit.

rachel: I'll roll back the tolerance to 2000ms now.

igor: I'll open a quick patch to session-manager to add a 1500ms dedupe guard for resume events (suppress metric and billing emission, respond 200 OK). Add unit tests.

maya: I'll hotpatch the metric-forwarder to preserve new labels and add a temporary dashboard panel: resume_attempt vs resume_ack lag by console_cohort and parser_mode. Also add an alert if tag-loss is detected during rollouts.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan: igor/patch/resume-dedupe -> staging at 11:45 UTC, maya/patch/metric-tags -> staging at 11:50 UTC, rachel/rollback/tolerance -> canary immediate.

ben: Long-term: billing should be gated on runtime resume_ack + stream_open confirmation (BILL-614). Console should warn if resume_tolerance < 500ms and require an explicit override. Also add e2e for partial-frame recovery paths in SDK tests so client libraries don't hammer resume.

rachel: Agreed. Once dice settle, we'll backfill queries to find affected tenants and notify CS.

ben: TL;DR: rollback tolerance, debounce resume, fix metric tags, billing guard. Prioritize debounce + metrics.
